annotation.method: Codex read the complete local paper, surveyed every formal claim, excluded experiments and delegated textbook results, searched the frozen mathlib and NumStability baselines, visually checked every selected formula page, and compiled private N/L proofs before accepting the targets.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P04 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 42, issue 3, 2020, printed pages C124-C141

rejected_candidates.reason: It is a useful intermediate bound, but Theorem 3.2 strictly extends it by treating inputs not already in the low precision.
It is explicitly a direct application of Theorem 3.1 and is less central than the selected input-conversion and LU-solve assemblies.
Its two conclusions are delegated to Higham's textbook Theorems 9.3 and 8.5 rather than proved in this paper.
Its factorization-stage coefficient is retained inside P04-T3, while Theorem 4.4 additionally connects it to the computed solution and is the stronger paper result.
The probabilistic statement is imported from another paper and the remaining comparisons use first-order or approximate language rather than exact finite claims.
They are empirical measurements rather than proof targets.

T1.decision: Use Algorithm 3.1's full indexed factorization and equation (3.4), retaining the distinct effective/internal gamma factors, q+b-1 right-to-left refinement, and zero-alpha same-precision specialization.

T2.decision: Use Theorem 3.2's exact mixed-input coefficient, combining two conversion errors with the block-FMA multiplication bound.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 4.4's factorization-plus-two-solves perturbation bridge and exact additional 2*gamma_n+gamma_n^2 term, absent from the frozen library's block-FMA surface.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject experiments, speed estimates, vague asymptotics, and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere.
Prefer exact displayed bounds and identities.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
